observation.visible_scene: Extreme macro close-up of a person's open eye (pale iris with a bright ring-light reflection on the cornea) and the surrounding skin, set against a pure black background. The eyelashes are beaded with many tiny clinging water droplets, and a larger droplet sits on the upper lid / brow skin.
visible_changes: A water droplet translates vertically downward through the left portion of the frame against the black background, entering near the top edge and exiting off the bottom edge; this downward falling pass repeats for a second droplet later in the excerpt.
The eye stays open and essentially motionless throughout; the iris, pupil and corneal highlight do not shift position.
The small droplets on the lashes and the droplet on the upper skin remain in roughly the same locations the whole time (persistent).
The framing and background do not visibly change, indicating the camera is static while only the droplet(s) move.
outside_clip_unknowns: The origin of the falling droplet(s) (whether they detach from the eye or lashes) and their landing point, since the top and bottom of the fall are partly outside the frame.
Whether more droplets continue to fall after the last sampled frame.
uncertain_details: Exact number of distinct falling droplets versus a single droplet re-entering; the segment clearly shows at least two separate downward passes.
Any minute horizontal drift of the falling droplet is small and not firmly measurable.
